| title = 8 [[Local government in the Philippines|LGU]]s | '''City''' | [[Tagaytay]] | '''Municipalities''' | [[Alfonso, Cavite|Alfonso]] | [[General Emilio Aguinaldo, Cavite|General Emilio Aguinaldo]] | [[Magallanes, Cavite|Magallanes]] | [[Maragondon]] | [[Mendez, Cavite|Mendez]] | [[Naic]] | [[Ternate, Cavite|Ternate]] }} | year = 2018 | members_label = Representative | members = [[Aniela Tolentino]] | blank1_name = Political party |blank1_info = {{Color box|{{party color|National Unity Party (Philippines)}}|border=darkgray}} [[National Unity Party (Philippines)|NUP]] | blank2_name = Congressional bloc | blank2_info = Majority }} '''Cavite's 8th congressional district''' is one of the eight [[congressional districts of the Philippines]] in [[Cavite]]. It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] since 2019.{{cite web |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316064243/http://congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |archive-date=March 16, 2017 |access-date=March 20, 2020 |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]]}} The district consists of the southern city of [[Tagaytay]] and the municipalities of [[Alfonso, Cavite|Alfonso]], [[General Emilio Aguinaldo, Cavite|General Emilio Aguinaldo]], [[Magallanes, Cavite|Magallanes]], [[Maragondon]], [[Mendez, Cavite|Mendez]], [[Naic]], and [[Ternate, Cavite|Ternate]], bordering the provinces of [[Batangas]] and [[Laguna (province)|Laguna]]. It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Aniela Tolentino]] of the [[National Unity Party (Philippines)|National Unity Party]] (NUP).{{cite web |title=House Members |url=https://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |access-date=February 1, 2023 |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]]}} The district was created in 2018 after [[General Trias]] became the sole component of [[Cavite's 6th congressional district|Cavite's 6th district]]. This change prompted the reorganization of the province's congressional districts: the former components of the 6th district, together with [[Indang]], became the new 7th district, while the areas that had comprised the old [[Cavite's 7th congressional district|7th district]], except for Indang, were reconstituted as the new 8th district. == Representation history == {| class="wikitable" ! rowspan="2" | # ! rowspan="2" colspan="2" | Image ! rowspan="2" | Member ! colspan="2" | Term of office ! rowspan="2" | Congress ! rowspan="2" | Party ! rowspan="2" | Electoral history ! rowspan="2" width="33%" | Constituent
